clue.text: Clothes items? Girls wear 'em possibly, but not I!

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of the three words may be rearranged into something else

parts.note: but not I says that one letter I is left over from the pool

explanation.surface: A remark that girls might wear these garments, though the speaker never would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals rearranging GIRLS WEAR EM, and 'but not I' says those letters make the answer once one I is set aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Knitted tubes worn over the calves are garments, the question mark admitting they are hardly full clothing.

clue.text: Mean deception in areas prone to flooding?

parts.note: mean in the sense of base or humble
telling falsehoods is deception

explanation.surface: Dishonest dealing going on in districts that keep getting flooded.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground sitting near sea level is the kind most liable to floods, hence the question mark for an example-style definition.

clue.text: Pilot's life's ending in ravine

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the ravine word

parts.note: a gorge is a ravine

indicators.note: ending picks the final letter of life's

explanation.surface: A pilot's life comes to an end down a ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending' takes E from 'life's'; 'in' puts it inside GORGE. George is old RAF slang for the automatic pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen's slang nickname for an aircraft's autopilot, a crossword-friendly sense of the name.

clue.text: Regular features of the grim academic session

indicators.note: regular features says take every other letter of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Typical marks of a gloomy period at university.
explanation.definitionFit: A school or university divides its year into these teaching periods, so a session of study.

clue.text: Some of the stuff in W.H. Smith not shifting, reportedly

definitions.text: Some of the stuff in W.H. Smith

indicators.note: reportedly says we hear a word that sounds like the one entered

parts.note: something not shifting is motionless, at rest

explanation.surface: Goods in a high-street shop that never move off the shelves.
explanation.walkthrough: W.H. Smith is a British high-street chain selling newspapers, books and writing materials.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper, envelopes and pens are among the goods that British chain sells, an example-style definition.

clue.text: Bookish types having some wine in Boston at lunchtime?

parts.note: liter is the American spelling of litre, a measure of wine in Boston
lunchtime is one o'clock, written as the numeral I

explanation.surface: Intellectuals enjoying a drop of wine over lunch in Boston.
explanation.walkthrough: Boston points to American spelling, LITER rather than LITRE; 'at lunchtime' is AT plus I, one o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A collective word for learned, well-read people, the intelligentsia.

clue.text: Little bird in water twice

parts.note: water as in urine, slang pee
a second slang word for urine, wee

explanation.surface: A small bird splashing about in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'water' is used twice, as two different childish words for urine.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the lapwing in some dialects, and of other small birds, so a little bird.

clue.text: Inhabitant of Madrid perhaps, not half cross

indicators.note: not half means only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: a person living in Madrid may be a native of Spain

explanation.surface: A Madrid resident who is not entirely angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' keeps the first four of SPANIARD's eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to cross a river is to bridge it, extend over it.

clue.text: Work in iron? It might have taken one to a Scottish forge

definitions.text: It might have taken one to a Scottish forge

indicators.note: in says the work word goes inside the iron word

parts.note: iron is an example of a chemical element, hence the query
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Metalworking at a Scottish smithy where couples once fled to wed.
explanation.walkthrough: Gretna Green, just over the Scottish border, had a blacksmith's forge where runaway English couples married.
explanation.definitionFit: Running away to marry secretly, as couples did by fleeing to Gretna Green's smithy.

clue.text: Yes, drink is said to get very cold

indicators.note: is said says the words are heard aloud

parts.note: aye is an old or Scottish word for yes; to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Agreeing to a drink and saying so.
explanation.walkthrough: AYE SUP spoken quickly sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb for becoming frozen over, as roads or wings do in frost.

clue.text: Two beasts that may get hot in the light

definitions.text: that may get hot in the light

parts.note: a wolf is a beast
a ram is a second beast

explanation.surface: A pair of animals warming up in the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: Tungsten, used for lamp filaments, is also called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for tungsten, the metal used for filaments that glow white-hot in light bulbs.

clue.text: What's excited a fan — one TV show's brilliant writer

indicators.note: excited says these letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A gushing fan asking what got them so worked up about a TV programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's' is just a link; 'excited' rearranges A FAN ONE TV SHOW. The answer is a nickname for Shakespeare, born at Stratford-upon-Avon.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Jonson's epithet for Shakespeare, the supreme dramatist from Stratford.

clue.text: Put up or knock down, might you say?

indicators.note: might you say asks us to hear the word, not read it

parts.note: to raze is to demolish a building

explanation.surface: A question about whether to build or demolish.
explanation.walkthrough: The two homophones mean opposite things: build up and pull down.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift or erect something, as one puts up a flag or building.

clue.text: Propagandist's hard work, always penning article

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the article goes inside

parts.note: a slog is a hard grind
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A spin doctor's toil, constantly writing pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' sets the article between the two other pieces; E'ER is the poetic contraction of ever.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who coins catchy slogans, usually for a political or commercial cause.

clue.text: Pedagogue thus restricts little children, only one left in charge

indicators.note: restricts means holds in, so the children go inside

parts.note: so means thus
ch is an abbreviation of child or children
the last one is the only one remaining

explanation.surface: A strict schoolmaster keeps the small children in check, leaving just one supervisor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricts' puts the children inside 'thus'. 'Pedagogue' is a noun here, so the answer is read as a noun, a schoolman.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolman, a teacher in the medieval scholarly tradition, as a noun.

clue.text: Like old recording that sounds authentic, excessively so?

indicators.note: sounds tells us the answer is heard as other words

parts.note: real means authentic; too real, authentic to excess

explanation.surface: An old recording that seems almost too genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes the open-spool tape machines used before cassettes.

clue.text: This ginger ale he brewed for a national organisation

indicators.note: brewed suggests the letters are cooked up into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A man has mixed up this ginger ale for a national body.
explanation.walkthrough: English Heritage is the body that looks after England's historic sites and monuments.
explanation.definitionFit: The charity caring for England's historic buildings is a country-wide body.

clue.text: Trendy theologian with rising reputation bound to be sought after

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: bound means tied round, so the theologian encloses the rest

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a good name is a reputation

explanation.surface: A fashionable divine with a growing name is certain to be popular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns the reputation word upwards, as suits a down clue, and 'bound' wraps the theologian's letters around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanted by many people, popular and much requested.

clue.text: After a jolly tea I start to rest in this?

definitions.text: After a jolly tea I start to rest in this?

parts.note: a Jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, RM
cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the word after

explanation.surface: Having had a jolly cup of tea, I settle in to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to' takes R from 'rest'. The whole clue is the definition: you rest in this chair after tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A comfortable chair with side supports, just the place to rest after tea.

clue.text: Solver's beginning to face setter's linguistic tricks in a duel?

indicators.note: to face means to stand in front of what follows
beginning picks the opening letter of Solver's

parts.note: a setter's puns and devices are wordplay

explanation.surface: The solver first confronts the compiler's verbal games in a battle of wits.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is sly: a duel with blades, not with puzzle clues.
explanation.definitionFit: Fencing with blades is what a duel involves, an example-style definition.

clue.text: See 12
First hint of diddling — issue to make one resign

indicators.note: first hint means the opening letter of diddling

parts.note: to emit is to issue

explanation.surface: A whiff of swindling forcing someone out of office.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal or Scots verb for giving up an office, relinquishing a post.

clue.text: Persist as fiery character

definitions.meaning: a fire-breathing mythical beast, or a fierce person

explanation.surface: Someone keeps going with a fiery temperament.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means continue tediously; as one it is the fire-breathing monster.

clue.text: Famous Dutchman's tots are backward

indicators.note: backward says the letters read from right to left

parts.note: tots are sums added up

explanation.surface: A celebrated Dutchman's young children are slow learners.
explanation.walkthrough: Erasmus of Rotterdam was the great Renaissance humanist scholar; 'backward' turns the whole phrase round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Renaissance humanist from Rotterdam is the most famous Netherlander scholar.

clue.text: Language not all readers enjoy

indicators.note: not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tongue that some readers dislike.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gaelic tongue of Scotland or Ireland, a crossword-favourite name.

clue.text: Monster turning on a child with ruler? Not these days!

definitions.text: Monster turning on a child with ruler? Not these days!

indicators.note: turning means the monster word is read backwards

parts.note: ET is the film alien, a monster
ER is Elizabeth Regina, a ruler

explanation.surface: A monstrous figure lashing out at a pupil with a ruler, which no longer happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes TE. The whole clue pictures an old-style schoolmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmaster striking a pupil with a ruler is a thing of the past.

clue.text: Hit — Engelbert's first record

parts.note: to tap is to hit lightly

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of Engelbert's

explanation.surface: A hit by Engelbert, his first disc.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnetic recording strip, or a recording made on one, is a sound record.

clue.text: Stirrer by and by must keep quiet

indicators.note: must keep means hold inside, so quiet goes in

parts.note: by and by means soon
p is piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: A troublemaker will soon have to be silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitchen utensil used to mix tea or soup, a whimsical sense of stirrer.

clue.text: In rally is talk off the cuff?

indicators.note: In says one piece sits inside another

parts.note: to rally is to recover, improve

explanation.surface: Is the speech at a rally unscripted?
explanation.definitionFit: To speak or act without preparation, inventing as one goes.
